description:
Delete the TypeScript port of the hierarchy resolver and drive the web graph view from the resolution fields the server now provides.

## Background

`web/src/utils/hierarchyResolution.ts:50-157` is a line-for-line TypeScript re-implementation of the Rust resolver, kept in sync only through the shared fixture `test-vectors/hierarchy_resolution.json`. `extractNodeType` in `web/src/utils/subgraphClustering.ts` re-parses `type:` prefixes from raw labels. The server's graph endpoint now ships resolved parent/children/cluster/rank and type per node, making both re-derivations dead weight and a semantic-drift risk.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-1: The graph view derives clustering, parent chains, and rank ordering from server-provided fields; `hierarchyResolution.ts` is deleted.
- [hard] REQ-2: Node type comes from the server payload; no client code parses `type:` label strings.
- [hard] REQ-3: The TypeScript vector test is removed with the port; the Rust vector test remains the fixture's sole consumer.
- [hard] REQ-4: Web lint, tests, and production build pass, and the graph view renders the same clusters for this repository's own tracker data as before the change.

## Notes

Update `web/src/types/models.ts` graph-node types to the new payload shape. If layout code assumed client-side memoization of resolution, move that caching behind the fetch layer rather than re-deriving.
title: Consume served hierarchy resolution in the web UI
